title: Ball Joint Replacement
summary: Suspension blueprint for confirming ball joint play, boot failure, and alignment impact before quoting replacement.
symptoms: Clunking or popping over bumps or while turning
Loose steering feel, wander, or pull
Uneven tire wear from changing suspension geometry
Visible torn boot, dry joint, or wheel play during inspection
inspect_first: Loaded and unloaded ball joint play using the correct method for the suspension design
Dust boot condition, grease loss, corrosion, and joint binding
Control arm bushings, tie rods, sway links, struts, and wheel bearing play
Tire wear and alignment angle concerns before pricing the repair
likely_causes: Worn press-in or bolt-in ball joint
Failed integrated ball joint in a control arm
Torn boot allowing contamination and grease loss
Impact damage or corrosion around the joint and mounting area
repair_overview: Confirm the failed joint and whether it is serviced separately or as part of the control arm.
Support the vehicle safely, unload the suspension as required, and remove the wheel.
Separate the joint from the knuckle without damaging the boot, sensor wiring, or tapered seat.
Press, bolt, or replace the joint/control arm, then torque fasteners to specification.
Recommend alignment when geometry is disturbed and road test for noise, pull, and steering feel.
common_mistakes: Checking ball joint play with the wrong suspension loading method
Quoting a separate joint when the vehicle uses an integrated control arm design
Damaging the knuckle taper or ABS wiring during separation
Skipping alignment after disturbing suspension geometry
estimate_guidance: Confirm whether the ball joint is serviced individually or bundled with a control arm.
Add alignment context when the repair affects camber, caster, toe, or steering centering.
Flag rust, seized pinch bolts, and press-in joint access as labor variables.
Quote paired repairs only when inspection shows both sides have play or matching wear.

recommended_repairs.description: Use when multiple front-end parts have possible play or the clunk source is not isolated.

recommended_repairs.title: Control Arm Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Common alternate path when the ball joint is integrated into the arm or the bushings are also worn.

recommended_repairs.title: Wheel Alignment
recommended_repairs.description: Recommended when suspension geometry or steering centering can change after the repair.

diagnostic_context.intro: Ball joint replacement should follow a loaded suspension inspection and a service-design check so the estimate matches the actual repair path.
